title: A city of arrivals
body: 来了就是深圳人 (lái le jiù shì Shēnzhèn rén)—“Once you arrive, you are a Shenzhener”—is a city slogan. Let it open a conversation: Zhou works here but grew up in Chengdu. Ask about her own story.

quiz.q: Zhou says she grew up in Chengdu. Which follow-up invites her story?
options: What brought you to Shenzhen?
So you only visit Shenzhen for holidays?
Then Shenzhen cannot feel like home to you?
quiz.why: Her hometown and her present home can both matter. Follow what she tells you.

title: A short greeting is enough
body: At this first pickup, you only need a greeting, your name and one clear question. 您好 (nín hǎo) offers a respectful opening; 你好 (nǐ hǎo) is a common everyday greeting. You can be warm without delivering a memorized speech.

quiz.q: You lose your place in a memorized introduction. What keeps the exchange going?
options: Use a short greeting and give your name
Restart the entire speech until every word is exact
Wait silently until Zhou introduces you for you
quiz.answer: Use a short greeting and give your name
quiz.why: A short accurate introduction leaves room to listen and respond.

title: Learn the name, not just the letters
body: On Lin’s contact screen, 林悦 (Lín Yuè) has both characters and pinyin. Ask her to say it, repeat it, and let her correct you. Pinyin helps you remember a name; it does not turn it into English spelling.
say: Learn the name, not just the letters

quiz.q: You can read Lín Yuè but are unsure how it sounds. What helps most?
options: Ask Lin to say it, then try it back
Use the English pronunciation of each letter
Avoid saying her name in every future conversation
quiz.answer: Ask Lin to say it, then try it back
quiz.why: Listening and checking are useful even when a spelling looks familiar.

title: Shenzhen has an older story
body: Nantou was an administrative and trading center long before Shenzhen’s modern technology boom. On a walk with Lin, old gates and busy streets give you something more personal to discuss than a company pitch. Ask what she likes about the neighborhood.

quiz.q: Which opening fits a walk through Nantou with Lin?
options: What do you enjoy about this neighborhood?
Was everything here built for the technology industry?
Can we skip your favorite places and discuss prices now?
quiz.answer: What do you enjoy about this neighborhood?
quiz.why: A specific question lets your host share their own experience of the place.

title: A cup and a conversation
body: Tea can be part of welcoming guests in homes and workplaces. In Lin’s workshop she offers tea before the tour. Thank her, say what you would like, and follow the conversation; accepting tea does not commit you to an order.

quiz.q: Lin offers tea, but you would prefer water. Which response fits?
options: Thank her and politely ask for water
Accept tea because a guest has no choice
Discuss the order quantity before answering the offer
quiz.answer: Thank her and politely ask for water
quiz.why: Hospitality leaves room for an ordinary preference.

title: Names and titles
body: 林 (Lín) is Lin Yue’s family name; 悦 (Yuè) is her given name. In a formal introduction, a surname plus role—such as 李经理 (Lǐ jīnglǐ), Manager Li—can be useful. Then use the form the person asks you to use.
src: Original language practice; cn-business contextual guidance

quiz.q: A manager introduces herself as 李经理 (Lǐ jīnglǐ). How can you address her initially?
options: 李经理 (Lǐ jīnglǐ)
经理李 (jīnglǐ Lǐ)
Use only an English name you choose for her
quiz.why: In this title pattern, the surname comes before the role.

title: The person behind the introduction
body: Zhou introduces Chen as a supplier from Huaqiangbei, the electronics-market area in Futian. That tells you where this connection began. Ask what his company supplies and what he handles; a market contact may have a different role from a factory manager.

quiz.q: You need someone to answer a component question. What should you establish first?
options: What Chen supplies and which questions he handles
Whether every Huaqiangbei seller makes the same product
Whether Zhou’s introduction guarantees the sample quality
quiz.answer: What Chen supplies and which questions he handles
quiz.why: A useful introduction gives you a starting point; a role question makes it actionable.

title: Where home is
body: Shenzhen’s welcoming civic slogan sits alongside many individual stories of home. Zhou tells you about Chengdu while working in Shenzhen. 家乡 (jiāxiāng), hometown, is a way into her story; listen to her answer rather than assigning tastes or habits by province.

quiz.q: Zhou mentions Chengdu. Which follow-up leaves room for her preferences?
options: What food do you miss from home?
You must want every meal very spicy, right?
So you will not enjoy Cantonese food, right?
quiz.answer: What food do you miss from home?
quiz.why: Ask about her experience. A place of origin does not decide a person’s tastes.

title: Cards and QR codes
body: Business cards still appear in introductions, and WeChat contact exchange is increasingly common. Chen offers his QR code. After adding him, a short message with your name and where you met helps connect the new contact to the real conversation.

quiz.q: Which first message helps Chen place you?
options: Your name and “We met at Lin’s studio today”
Only “Hello” with no identifying detail
A long quotation request without an introduction
quiz.answer: Your name and “We met at Lin’s studio today”
quiz.why: Give the new contact enough context to recognize you.

title: Who handles this?
body: At Lin’s hardware studio, the founder, supplier and tester handle different parts of the project. 谁负责测试？ (shéi fùzé cèshì?)—“Who handles testing?”—is a useful way to learn the team, without guessing authority from age or how much someone speaks.

quiz.q: Zhou says she organizes testing, while Lin approves changes. Who should receive a test-schedule question first?
options: Zhou, who organizes testing
Lin solely because she is the founder
Chen solely because he introduced himself first
quiz.why: Follow the responsibility the team actually described.

title: Meet at the exit
body: “At the station” can leave two people searching for each other. In this Futian meeting, Zhou sends 三号出口 (sān hào chūkǒu), Exit 3. Reply with your exit and a nearby sign. Treat the exit here as a practice detail, then use the actual signs when traveling.

quiz.q: Zhou is at Exit 3 and you are at Exit 2. Which message helps coordinate?
options: I am at Exit 2; shall I come to Exit 3?
I have arrived, with no exit detail
I am at Exit 3, because that is your meeting point
quiz.answer: I am at Exit 2; shall I come to Exit 3?
quiz.why: State your actual location before agreeing how to meet.

title: Read the address in layers
body: Shekou is in Nanshan District, across Shenzhen Bay from Hong Kong. In an address, the district and neighborhood orient you; a building name, floor and entrance finish the job. Keep 蛇口 (Shékǒu) visible on your phone when confirming the place.

quiz.q: Lin says the office is in Shekou. What would make the address usable?
options: The building and entrance, as well as the neighborhood
Only the word Shenzhen
Only her home province
quiz.answer: The building and entrance, as well as the neighborhood
quiz.why: A district or neighborhood is wider than one meeting place.

title: Confirm the whole appointment
body: A friendly 三点半见 (sān diǎn bàn jiàn)—“See you at half past three”—works when both people share the context. If your messages cover several days, confirm the day and whether it is morning or afternoon. Precision makes it easier to be considerate.

quiz.q: You have only “3:30” in a message spanning two days. What should you confirm?
options: Which day and morning or afternoon
Only whether tea will be served
Only the neighborhood’s Chinese spelling
quiz.answer: Which day and morning or afternoon
quiz.why: A time needs a shared day and part of the day.

title: Make room for a neighborhood walk
body: Shekou includes older neighborhoods as well as modern business spaces. Near Chiwan, Tianhou Temple is associated with Mazu, a sea goddess. If Lin suggests a walk, ask what she wants to show you and agree a time that works for both of you.
say: Make room for a neighborhood walk

quiz.q: Lin offers a neighborhood walk on Friday, but your supplier visit may run late. What works best?
options: Explain the timing conflict and propose a workable time
Accept immediately and decide later whether to appear
Decline because a walk cannot help a business relationship
quiz.answer: Explain the timing conflict and propose a workable time
quiz.why: Interest and a realistic plan go together. A social invitation does not require overpromising.

title: One message everyone can use
body: Before leaving, send one short recap: day, time, place and entrance. Ask the other person to confirm a mismatch. This is especially helpful while learning Mandarin: a written name or number can settle something you did not catch by ear.

quiz.q: Your calendar and Zhou’s message disagree about both day and entrance. What should the recap do?
options: Name both conflicting details and ask which is correct
Repeat only the time, which already matches
Choose your calendar’s version without asking
quiz.answer: Name both conflicting details and ask which is correct
quiz.why: Point to the actual differences so the reply can resolve them.
